summary: Configured a persistent three-member MariaDB Galera cluster. All members are active/enabled, Primary, Synced, Ready, at cluster size 3, with identical data and commit position. A node3 outage preserved a writable two-member quorum; node3 automatically recovered missing writes by IST after normal startup.
actions_performed: Installed MariaDB 10.11, Galera 4, and rsync on node1, node2, and node3.
Configured shared cluster membership with unique node identities, node-IP listeners, InnoDB row replication, rsync SST, and recoverable gcache.
Verified writes submitted through each member were readable from every other member.
Stopped node3, wrote through both surviving members, restored node3, verified automatic resynchronization, then successfully wrote through node3 again.

evidence.summary: All configurations use the same three-address gcomm peer list with unique node identities. Final checks show all enabled services active in one Primary, Synced, Ready cluster of size 3.

evidence.requirement: Writes through any member are available from the other members
evidence.summary: Writes committed through node1, node2, and node3. Final direct TCP reads on every member returned the same six test rows, including the post-rejoin node3 write, at wsrep_last_committed=22.

evidence.requirement: Remain available with one member unavailable and automatically resynchronize it on return
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline showed three Synced members. During node3's confirmed service outage, node1/node2 remained Primary and Ready at size 2 and accepted replicated writes. Normal node3 startup received four missing writesets by IST (seqnos 18–21), transitioned to Synced, and restored identical data and cluster size 3.
